newsitem.title: MEXICO: Hylsamex sees 1997 steel output up 6 pct.
newsitem.headline: Hylsamex sees 1997 steel output up 6 pct.

text.p: Mexican steel producer Hylsamex said on Thursday that its output would increase by at least 6.0 percent in 1997.
The company said that it expected production of about 2.4 million tons in 1996.
"We should be expecting growth between six and 10 percent for 1997," said Rafael Rubio, assistant director of economic studies for the company, a subsidiary of Grupo Alfa.
He said domestic demand for steel products was growing and that that trend could accelerate in 1997.
Rubio said that the company was still considering a placement of $100 million in capital markets.
"This offer depends on our financial needs, on what we will need for our investment programs, and up to this time we don't really need to go to the capital markets," he said.
